title: Artificial Intelligence Applied to UAVs & Its Impact on Humanitarian Action
html:
As shown in Gartner’s Hype Cycle graph, technologies tend to go through a predictable path to adoption. But, the promise of something like Artificial Intelligence has been around for decades. I even remember studying it back in university ~25 years ago. Although the past few years have shown some tangible advancements, I have few examples of how it is being used systematically in the humanitarian sector.

In late 2019, Camille Oren joined me and expressed an interest in UAVs. We discussed OCHA’s 2014 report on the topic and wondered what had changed in the 5 years since. After raising my question of seeing tangible examples of AI applications in the humanitarian sector, Camille suggested joining the two topics.

Combining a literature review and interviews with UAV experts from both the private and humanitarian sectors, we wanted to draft a report that aimed to highlight the extent to which AI increased the capabilities of drones. The resulting paper covers topics such as how AI has already been used in UAVs, how it is being trialled, and how it may be used in the future; how AI use in UAVs should be approached ethically; and a variety of case studies.

Although lengthy, Artificial Intelligence Applied to Unmanned Aerial Vehicles And its Impact on Humanitarian Action does a great service to outline the amazing impact AI is having and will have on UAV use in our sector.
